name: deviation_from_ema_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Price acts like a rubber band around the EMA(50) on 1-min bars. When price deviates more than 1.5 * ATR(14) from EMA(50), the elastic tendency of mean reversion kicks in. The EMA(50) represents the last ~50 minutes of trend, and deviations beyond 1.5 ATR are unsustainable accelerations that typically revert to the EMA within 20-30 bars. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders use EMAs as directional trend indicators (above EMA = bullish) rather than measuring the distance FROM the EMA as a mean reversion signal. The distance-from-EMA approach treats the EMA as a magnet rather than a traffic light. This edge persists because measuring deviation from EMA requires additional computation beyond standard crossover logic.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 30 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: ema_slope > -0.01 * close (EMA not in strong downtrend)
long.confirmation: ema_dev_atr[t] > ema_dev_atr[t-1] (deviation narrowing, starting to snap back)

conditions: ema_slope < 0.01 * close (EMA not in strong uptrend)
short.confirmation: ema_dev_atr[t] < ema_dev_atr[t-1] (deviation narrowing, starting to snap back)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: 2.5 * ATR(14) from EMA(50) — if deviation extends to 2.5 ATR, thesis broken
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * ATR(14) once past 60% of target
exit.signal_exit: exit if ema_dev_atr makes new extreme beyond ±2.5 ATR

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; normalize by ATR(14)/close across stocks

filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (EMA(50) needs 50 bars) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: ema_slope should be near-flat — strong trend regimes make reversion unreliable
filters.event_filter: skip on earnings day for the stock
other_filters: skip if NIFTY 50 has moved >1.5% from open (strong market trend day)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — concept is simple but ATR-normalized deviation adds a layer vs raw EMA reversion

weaknesses: EMA(50) on 1-min = 50 minutes; this is a compromise between responsiveness and stability but may be too short
The 1.5 ATR threshold is data-mined-looking — needs robust out-of-sample validation across different market regimes
Stop loss at 2.5 ATR from EMA means potentially large per-trade loss relative to target, hurting the W:L ratio
prior_art: Mean reversion to moving averages is a foundation of TA (Murphy, 'Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets'). ATR-normalized deviation is similar to the 'Kase Bar' concept. Connors' research on price distance from MA as a reversion predictor (daily timeframe) is directly relevant. The rubber band analogy is from Linda Raschke.
notes: Edge math: 0.56 * 45bps - 0.44 * 37.5bps = 25.2 - 16.5 = 8.7 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -2.3 bps. Slightly negative. Need to either tighten stop (reduce to 2.0 ATR) to improve W:L or add confluence filter (e.g., VWAP agreement) to push win rate to 0.60+.
